claims.statement: Writers can create/edit CODEOWNERS and be owners; requiring approval needs an admin/owner. Availability is public Free or public/private Pro/Team/Enterprise. Named owners need write access; teams must be visible and have explicit TEAM write access even if individual members already have write.

Owners are requested on owned changes once a PR is ready; draft PRs do not automatically request them. Converting back to draft does not unsubscribe prior owners. Required code-owner approval is a separate optional protection setting.
Tooltips and product-specific screenshots illustrate ownership visibility, not independently verified owner permissions or binary-image assurance.
CODEOWNERS lookup uses the FIRST file found in .github/, root, then docs/, rather than merging files. Ownership is branch-specific; gh-pages and main can use different owners.

The PR BASE branch CODEOWNERS determines review requests. Fork PRs targeting upstream use upstream ownership; those targeting the fork use fork ownership, and named owners must have write access to that fork. Tooltips reflect the displayed branch.
CODEOWNERS must be under 3 MB; an oversized file is not loaded and does not request owners. Wildcard consolidation is suggested to reduce size, but file existence alone proves no routing.
CODEOWNERS does not support escaped leading #, ! negation, or [] character ranges from gitignore syntax. An ordinary gitignore parser is not equivalent.
Patterns are followed by users or @org/team with explicit write permissions. Only organization teams are supported; enterprise teams are not, where that feature distinction applies.
Multiple owners for the same pattern must appear on one line. Repeated patterns on different lines retain only the last match.
Email ownership is generally possible, but FPT/GHEC managed-user accounts cannot be referenced by email. The source gives no reason for that limitation.

Matching is case-sensitive even on macOS. Invalid lines are skipped and can be inspected through UI/API errors; nonexistent or insufficient-permission owners are not assigned. A partly valid file is not blanket correct.

Examples illustrate default * ownership, last-match precedence, inline comments, email Go owners and an explicitly writable organization team for txt. These owner handles and patterns are examples, not adopted local identities.

Examples distinguish root build/logs, docs/* immediate entries, apps/ at any depth, /docs/ root subtree, /scripts/ with two alternative owners, and **/logs across depths. Matching depth and anchoring must be tested for actual changed files.

An /apps/github line with NO owners overrides /apps ownership and removes code-owner routing; a later specific line with another owner instead replaces the earlier owner. A presence check would miss both effects.
Protected branches can separately require code-owner approval. Approval by ANY listed owner is enough when multiple owners share the affected pattern; all listed owners are not required.

Protect the CODEOWNERS file itself (or its .github directory) with an appropriate owner. The source suggests rulesets as an alternative, but these configuration suggestions do not prove comprehensive unauthorized-change prevention.
Further-reading destinations remain references; no additional artifact review is credited for following a link.

scope: Full pinned article plus literal dependency reading; source evidence only, without adoption or live behavior verification.
